findings.claim: No item fixes the shutdown phase in which NaruServe closes open SSE streams. Because D-335 writes SSE as an ordinary chunked response on the worker, TinyHttpd's stop() does not close these streams: onServerStopping closes only TinyHttpd's own SseStream and upgraded connections, and stop() then waits until the grace deadline. If wave 7 registers SSE closing as a force-close participant (after the adapter stop), any shutdown with an open SSE stream lasts the full timeout and clients get no close notice first. That goes against object.md §11.4 step 3, which says to notify SSE/WS while short requests drain.
findings.suggested_fix: State in D-401/D-341 that SSE closing (ending the drain loop and running onClose) is a before-wait participant, so the adapter stop only waits for short HTTP exchanges.

findings.claim: D-435 aborts, once, only sessions whose sender-executor write has been in flight for more than 1 s. Two cases still block TinyHttpd's stop thread. First, TinyHttpd's read thread writes Ping (keepalive) and Pong frames under the same writeLock, outside the sender executor. Second, a write that is under 1 s old at check time can then stall. TinyHttpd's stop() calls fireStop, which does close(1001) under writeLock, for every upgraded connection before its grace loop and outside the deadline. So one such stalled session holds shutdown until the 30 s write timeout, which breaks the timeout-plus-margin bound of D-344/T44.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the D-435 ResponseWrapper return a wrapping UpgradedConnection whose OutputStream records write start for every writer, read thread included. Make the before-wait participant abort every session that has any write in flight (no 1 s threshold), or keep a watchdog running until the adapter stop's onServerStopping loop has passed.

findings.claim: D-431 makes req.body(Class/TypeRef) @Nullable, so in Kotlin it returns T?. The kotlin.md example `val body = req.body(CreateUserRequest::class.java); val name = body.name` then no longer compiles, yet D-349 requires every docs/api Kotlin example to compile and run as a test. D-192 lists kotlin.md for update but names no example rewrite.
findings.suggested_fix: Have wave 5 rewrite the Kotlin examples that dereference req.body(...) (safe call, or the D-354 reified extension) when it applies D-431, and set the kotlin.md nullability row to T?.

findings.claim: D-435 only aborts sessions whose NaruServe sender write has been in flight for more than 1 s, but TinyHttpd's stop path can still block the stopping thread for up to the 30 s write timeout per session. Three cases are not covered: (a) the read loop's own Ping (sent after an idle interval) or Pong reply is stalled on a full send buffer while holding writeLock, and NaruServe cannot see that write; (b) a sender write started less than 1 s before the participant ran; (c) no write is in flight but the peer's receive window is full, so the 1001 close frame that fireStop writes on the stopping thread blocks. HttpServer.stop calls onServerStopping -> Upgraded.fireStop -> WebSocket.close(1001) one connection at a time, before its grace loop starts, so each stalled session can add up to writeTimeout. That breaks the timeout-plus-1.5 s margin of D-344 and makes T44 with stalled clients flaky.
findings.evidence: /Users/beom/work/git/TinyHttpd/websocket/src/main/java/com/snoworca/tinyhttpd/websocket/WebSocket.java:181-200 (close writes under writeLock), :288 and :360 (read-loop ping/pong under writeLock); /Users/beom/work/git/TinyHttpd/core/src/main/java/com/snoworca/tinyhttpd/server/HttpServer.java:468-470 (serial onServerStopping before grace loop); Connection.java:508-520 (fireStop synchronous); docs/research/naruserve-v1/design/00.design.md:584 (D-435), :585 (D-344)
findings.suggested_fix: In the before-wait participant, have NaruServe send close 1001 itself for every session, each on its sender slot or a bounded worker, and call UpgradedConnection.close() (abortSocket) on every session whose close write has not finished within a short fixed bound (e.g. 1 s), however old any earlier write is. TinyHttpd's later fireStop -> close() then returns at once because closeSent is set or the socket is aborted. Add a T44 case: a peer that stops reading after filling its window and is otherwise idle, plus a peer stalled on a server Ping.

findings.claim: D-425 closes idle sessions from NaruServe's single scheduler thread. WebSocket.close takes writeLock and writes a frame, so a session whose socket is stalled (for example on a TinyHttpd read-loop Ping into a full buffer) blocks that thread for up to the 30 s write timeout. While it is blocked, every other session's idle timeout is late, which works against the isolation that D-320 asks for on the send side.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the scheduler only mark the session and hand the close 1001 to that session's sender slot (D-417), or abort the socket through UpgradedConnection.close() when the close does not finish within a bound. Keep the scheduler thread free of socket writes.

findings.claim: TinyHttpd caps each header line at inputBufferBytes - 2, not only the request line. D-414 sizes inputBufferBytes from the request-line limit alone. If the header-size configuration of D-225 is raised, a single header line longer than 8190 bytes (a large Cookie) still gets 431, even though the configured header size allows it.
findings.suggested_fix: Either derive inputBufferBytes as max(8192, requestLineLimit + 2, the per-header-line limit + 2), or record in docs/api/defaults.md that one header line is limited to inputBufferBytes - 2, separately from the total header size.

findings.claim: D-426 says shutdown during STARTING waits up to its timeout for listen() to end. It does not say what shutdown returns or reports, or which state is visible, when the timeout passes while onStart is still blocked. It also does not say whether the path goes through FAILED before TERMINATED, which D-427 and the object.md §11.3 diagram (STARTING -fail-> FAILED -> TERMINATED) distinguish.
findings.suggested_fix: State the result of shutdown when its timeout passes during STARTING (return normally with the app still STARTING and pending stop recorded, or throw a timeout), and state whether a pending-stop listen() passes through FAILED.
